title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Sentencing Circumstances such as Surrender and Meritorious Performance in Duty-Related Crime Cases

articles.content_en:
III. Determination and Handling of Truthful Confession of Criminal Facts
Where a criminal suspect does not constitute voluntary surrender according to law, but truthfully confesses the criminal facts and falls under any of the following circumstances, a light punishment may be given as appropriate: (1) the case-handling authority has grasped part of the criminal facts, and the criminal suspect confesses other criminal facts of the same kind; (2) the evidence grasped by the case-handling authority is insufficient, and the criminal suspect's truthful confession helps to collect evidence for conviction.
Where a criminal suspect truthfully confesses the criminal facts and falls under any of the following circumstances, a light punishment shall generally be given: (1) the case-handling authority has only grasped a small part of the criminal facts, and the criminal suspect confesses most of the criminal facts of the same kind that are not grasped; (2) the truthful confession plays an important role in the collection of evidence for conviction.

IV. Handling of Recovery of Illicit Money and Goods, etc.
Where all or most of the illicit money and goods are recovered in embezzlement cases, a light punishment shall generally be considered.
Where all or most of the illicit money and goods are recovered in bribery cases, a light punishment may be given as appropriate according to the specific circumstances.
Where the criminal suspect or his/her relatives and friends voluntarily return the illicit money and goods or actively cooperate in the process of recovery by the case-handling authority, such situation shall be distinguished from the recovery of illicit money and goods ex officio by the case-handling authority during the investigation of the case when sentencing.
After the filing of a case for duty-related crimes, economic losses that are recovered by the criminal suspect or his/her relatives and friends on their own, economic losses recovered by the judicial authority, the unit to which the criminal suspect belongs, or its superior competent department, or economic losses reduced due to objective reasons shall not be deducted, but may be regarded as a circumstance for a light punishment as appropriate.
